stimuli.description: Immersive Virtual Environments (IVEs) of a university classroom with three different illuminance levels: 100 lx, 300 lx, and 500 lx.

tables.description: Statistical treatments for Phase 1 (IVE validation) and Phase 2 (psychological and neurophysiological responses).
Mean and standard deviation of sense of presence for each item of the SUS questionnaire across different illuminance levels.

limitations: Time of day was not controlled due to large sample size requirements.

Only illuminance level was varied; other lighting variables (e.g., uniformity, color temperature) were kept constant, limiting a comprehensive understanding of human responses to VR-based lighting environments.
Only one classroom design was used, limiting generalizability to different classroom designs.
VR might induce students to focus more on enjoying the experience rather than correctly performing the task.
The presence of other students and different viewpoint positions within the classroom were excluded due to parameterization difficulties, potentially influencing task performance.
